Figure 7. Examples of more spatial tasks that can be created using our data generation pipeline.

Figure 1. (a) Furniture Assembly Example. Top Left: Many real-world objects do not lend themselves to simple natural language description. The table on the right can be described using fundamental convex shapes and their bounding boxes but the chair on the left has non-convex parts without an analytical expression. Thus it is preferable to include visual information. Top Right: Oftentimes, single-view observation leads to visual misconceptions and does not reveal certain alignment issues. The chair looks well-assembled in the view shown on the left but when it turns to the view shown on the right we see the backrest is slightly misplaced in the X-axis. Bottom: Only using the bounding box dimensions, we are unable to assemble furniture that has non-convex parts. In the left instance, the bounding boxes are perfectly aligned but the assembly is problematic. A good assembly example is shown on the right.
